title: Deep learning screening of otoscopic images for ENT referral: development, validation and deployment of NHREF OtoScan
summary: A MobileNetV2 screening model for ENT referral achieved 97.0% sensitivity and 75.6% specificity on 718 held-out otoscopic images. The retrospective evaluation used near-duplicate grouping and found source-dependent performance. The authors report no prospective clinical validation or clinician comparison; the software is described as research use with mandatory specialist review.
organization: Nawaloka Hospitals Research and Education Foundation, Colombo, Sri Lanka

evidence.tested: On a held-out set of 718 otoscopic images, the frozen referral threshold yielded 97.0% sensitivity and 75.6% specificity. Images were grouped to reduce near-duplicate leakage; performance varied by source dataset.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective public-image validation only; no prospective clinical validation or comparison against clinicians. The paper says the system is research software, not a medical device, and requires specialist review.
evidence.ai_role: A calibrated MobileNetV2 model estimates abnormal-ear probability to support an ENT-referral screening decision.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
